title: LLM API Rapid Response QA Playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, consumable reference for AE/SDR/SE to handle common buyer questions and objections when competing against general LLM API providers (public hosted-only vendors, single-model endpoints, and companies that emphasize model access instead of serving). Not a full battlecard—this is a fast Q&A playbook for real-time calls and async rebuttals.

Primary audience:
- AE/SE in discovery and POC stage
- Product-marketing creating concise talking points for demos
- Solutions engineers needing quick scripts for Slack/email follow-ups

Top-level positioning pillars (one-line each):
1) Serving economics: We treat inference as a systems problem — predictable per-token economics via batching, caching, and routing controls, not just model pricing.
2) Production fidelity: We give teams the same API surface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so SLAs, observability and rollouts map directly to customer ops.
3) Operational safety & flexibility: Built-in fallbacks, canary rollouts, and private deployment options reduce business risk when models change.

Competitive snapshot (who we see most):
- OpenAI / Large hosted-first providers: Strengths = fast time-to-test, model innovation. Weaknesses = limited deployment modes, limited cost controls, vendor lock-in concerns and black-box performance at scale.
- Anthropic / Safety-first APIs: Strengths = model safety framing, strong research messaging. Weaknesses = fewer deployment flavors, limited runtime controls for cost/throughput tradeoffs.
- Hugging Face / Model marketplace: Strengths = model variety and community. Weaknesses = inconsistent runtime SLAs, unclear productionization path for enterprises.
- Cohere / Embedding & text-first providers: Strengths = targeted capabilities (embeddings). Weaknesses = narrower operational story vs multi-variant serving and rollout tooling.
- Self-hosted runtimes (Replicate, open-source stacks): Strengths = control, lower sticker cost if you operate well. Weaknesses = ops burden, tooling gaps, need to reimplement monitoring and rollout patterns.

Feature axes buyers care about (how to frame differences quickly):
- Latency predictability: call out 95th/99th percentile figures and that we expose route-level SLOs and alerting.
- Unit cost control: emphasize batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization profiles as levers we expose vs vendor who only sells model access.
- Deployment modes: highlight Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) as a unique triad.
- Observability & debugging: token-level cost breakdowns, trace hooks, example logs for hallucination/regression debugging.
- Rollouts & reliability: canaries, A/B deployments, automatic fallbacks to cheaper/compatible variants under capacity pressure.

Common buyer traps and our red flags (what to call out to prospects):
- "Model access solves serving": customers assume model access = production-readiness. Red flag: no rollout/fallback or detailed latency SLOs.
- "Lower per-token price is cheaper overall": vendors quote per-token model price but lack batching/cache; end result higher TCO. Red flag: no batching or KV cache docs/benchmarks.
- "We’ll self-host to avoid vendor lock-in": self-hosting is attractive but ops cost, SLAs, and scaling complexity often get underestimated. Red flag: lack of SRE runbooks and cost model.
- "All models behave the same in prod": customers underestimate quality drift and evaluation needs. Red flag: no eval hooks or prompt-set regression alerts.

Top objections and short rebuttals (soundbites + supporting detail):
1) Objection: "We already use [hosted provider], simpler to keep going."
   Rebuttal: "Totally — fast proof-of-concept makes sense. If you care about predictable cost and SLAs at scale, we let you keep the same API while adding routing, caching and dedicated capacity so your app doesn't get surprised when usage grows."

   Supporting detail: Example: for a doc summarization flow, our KV/prefix caching and batching reduced per-inference token cost by 35% in a customer POC while keeping 95%ile latency under 200ms.

2) Objection: "Why not self-host? Cheaper in the long run."
   Rebuttal: "Self-hosting can be cheaper only if you bake operational maturity into your stack — autoscaling, eviction policies, observability, quiet hours for retraining validations, and security integrations. We provide those controls as config and hand over operational runbooks for private deployments."

   Supporting detail: Point to our Dedicated customers who ran a TCO comparison: after including SRE headcount and storage egress, break-even was >18 months for modest traffic.

3) Objection: "We need the newest models immediately."
   Rebuttal: "We surface new model variants fast and let you route by policy — but the difference is we let you roll new models to a fraction of traffic with automatic fallback to prior variant if latency or quality drifts."

   Supporting detail: Demo suggestion: show a canary deploy, inject a synthetic regression, and show automatic fallback and alerting in console.

Rapid call scripts (30–60s responses):
- If asked about cost: "Most vendors quote model tokens. We price and optimize the serving path — batching, caching and model variants are first-class which reduces your per-request cost without sacrificing latency. We’ll show you where your tokens are going in the console."
- If asked about reliability: "We offer SLA-backed Dedicated pools, private control plane options, and built-in fallbacks so your app degrades gracefully rather than failing hard."
- If asked about lock-in: "Our API and deployment abstraction were built so customers can start hosted and later move to Dedicated/Private without rewriting application logic."

Demo / play suggestions (what to show in 10–20 min):
1) Quick perf dashboard: 95/99 latency, token-level cost, per-route breakdown.
2) Canary flow: deploy variant B to 10% traffic, show regression alert, trigger fallback to A.
3) Cost-improvement demo: show same prompt served with and without KV cache + batching and the delta in token/latency.

Collateral snippets for emails and decks (one-liners):
- "Predictable inference economics — controls over batching, caching, and model variants, not just model pricing."
- "Same API, three deployment modes: test in hosted, scale on Dedicated, secure in Private."
- "Safeguard your product: canaries, rollbacks, and automatic fallbacks to contain model drift and capacity outages."

Frequently asked technical questions (fast answers):
- Q: "How do you handle long-run latencies from large-context models?"
  A: "We adapt kernel selection and batching by sequence-length distribution and can route heavy requests to variants optimized for long context windows to protect 95th percentile latency."
- Q: "Do you support KMS/HSM for Private?"
  A: "Yes — customer-managed KMS integrations are supported for Private deployments and Dedicated customers can request HSM-backed key storage."

Next steps for AE/SEs:
- Keep a checklist in CRM: specify expected traffic patterns (seq length, QPS), required latency SLO, data residency/security needs.
- Offer a short POC: 2-week perf + cost experiment (two workflows: hosted trial with sample traffic; optional Dedicated trial with real routing policies).
- If buyer is sensitive to price: propose a batching + cache pilot first — often largest near-term unit cost wins.

Open items / TODOs (internal):
- Add 95/99 latency benchmark slide for the common model families (LLama2-like, Falcon-like) across our Hosted and Dedicated tiers (owner: Evan).
- Capture two recent customer case studies with actual TCO deltas (owner: Maya).
- Create 1-page PDF cheat sheet for SDRs with 3 soundbites, 2 quick numbers, and the checklist (owner: Samir).

Notes to self / rapid scripts to save in Slack snippets:
- "If they care about compliance: \"We can run a Private control plane so you keep audit logs and KMS integration in your environment.\""
- "If they care about model freshness: \"We set canaries for new variants and automatically route around regressions.\""

End of playbook. Keep this doc short and iterate after each competitive loss — capture verbatim customer quotes and update the rebuttals with real metrics.
